dedupe_keys.name: care to compare wind turbine scada data for early fault detection

description: This data set is a labelled benchmark for detecting wind turbine faults early from SCADA data. It was published by Christian Gück and Cyriana Roelofs with the paper "CARE to Compare: A real-world dataset for anomaly detection in wind turbine data", which also defines the CARE score for evaluating detectors, because public benchmarks with real labelled faults were lacking. It holds 95 data sets with 89 years of SCADA time series from 36 turbines at three wind farms: farm A is five onshore turbines in Portugal based on the EDP open data platform, with 86 features, and farms B and C are anonymised offshore farms in Germany with 257 and 957 features. Of the 95 data sets, 45 end in a labelled anomaly event leading to a turbine fault and 50 show normal behaviour, with turbine-status labels per data point and some fault details. Files are CSV, one per data set, in a ZIP of about 5.5 GB downloadable from Zenodo under CC BY-SA 4.0 at no cost; the record was updated in September 2026. Caveats: power data were scaled for anonymity, and minimum, maximum and standard deviation values contain implausible entries. Simulation uses are testing fault detection and condition monitoring methods for wind fleets. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
name: CARE to Compare: wind turbine SCADA data for early fault detection

sources.note: Paper, 95 data sets, 36 turbines, 3 farms, features, 45/50 split, known issues, CC-BY-SA-4.0
